title: Trump Administration Preparing $2.8 Billion Sale of 2,000-Pound Bombs to Israel
detail: The Trump administration on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, informally notified Congress of a planned $2.8 billion sale to Israel of 40,000 907-kg (2,000-pound) bombs — 20,000 MK-84 general-purpose bombs and 20,000 BLU-117s (a thermally coated variant for safer naval storage), plus I-2000 Penetrator warheads designed to strike hardened, underground targets. It would be the largest single sale of the munition in recent years and is financed mostly through US foreign military financing, meaning American taxpayer dollars fund Israel's purchase of the US-made weapons. The Biden administration paused delivery of these bombs in 2023 over concerns about mass-casualty risk in Gaza; Trump lifted that hold on returning to office. The sale drew immediate criticism, with Sen. Chris Van Hollen vowing to work to block it and accusing the administration of 'sending bombs paid for by American taxpayers to a government led by a wanted war criminal.'

media.caption: The Trump administration is preparing the largest single sale of 2,000-pound bombs to Israel in recent years

title: State Department Reallocates $52 Million in Military Aid From Europe, Middle East to Latin America
detail: The Trump administration on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, reallocated $52 million in US military assistance away from Slovakia, North Macedonia, Tunisia and Iraq to Panama, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia, with the State Department saying the funds would help 'combat narcoterrorism in our backyard' and continue securing the Panama Canal. The shift reflects the administration's renewed emphasis on the Western Hemisphere and closer ties with right-leaning Latin American governments under a revived Monroe Doctrine framing; it follows Secretary of State Marco Rubio's visit the prior week to Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, where he pledged additional US support against drug trafficking and illegal immigration.

media.caption: The State Department shifted $52 million in military aid from European and Middle Eastern allies to four Latin American countries
